l.i: in ea, cum sit tanti ponderis, discutienda de-
sudare, ut veneno antidotum, longè latea[?]
per venas Christiani orbis grassanti, eo ve-
locius & valentius possit obuiare. Non sum
nescius, viros grauissimos, tam è nostris
Iacobo duce) in hanc palestram iampri-
pariter non possit nō destruere, cum rectum
semel dicam quod res est) cum me measq;
Olympi compegerim, non fuit cur in erro-
rum dissoluendis nebulis, aut ventis con-
rem. Hic nulla in regibus coercendis populi
tempestas, Papismi caligo nulla. Paulò in-
ferius quidem, ad medium huius montis,

page.notes: Doubtful: "latea" (line 3) is uncertain, possibly "latet" or "latè" followed by a mark; a reference mark stands near it. "measq;" has a small mark after "meas" that may be a superscript q; rendered as "measq;". Faint marks in the right margin near the lines "per venas" and "meas" are not text. The "Epistola Dedicatoria." running head has no page number printed.
